unit_operations.name: Production Bioreactor (Step 3)
unit_operations.purpose: Fed-batch production culture; inoculated to target initial VCC and cultivated under controlled temperature, pH and DO; bolus nutrient feed NF-1 plus multiple glucose feeds to keep glucose >1.0 g/L; antifoam up to 100 ppm. Only upstream step identified as impacting product quality; sole step defining the upstream design space.
unit_operations.scale: Commercial 15,000 L working volume (Process 2 scaled from 5,000 L Ph3 and 1,000 L clinical; Process 1 500-1,000 L). Design space defined on qualified 2 L scale-down model.
unit_operations.source_pages: pp. 61-93 (Tables 3.9-3.20, Figures 3.2-3.9); DOE ranges Table 3.14 p.77; response-surface Table 3.16 p.80; CQA limits Table 3.17 p.81; design-space inequalities/bounds p.90; control strategy Fig 3.9 p.93

process_parameters.notes: No quality impact

process_parameters.name: Inoculum In Vitro Cell Age
process_parameters.notes: No quality impact

param_cqa_relationships: Response-surface (2nd-order polynomial, scaled estimates per half-range, p<0.05) Table 3.16: Temperature -> aFuc -0.62, Galactosylation +1.67, CEX Acidic Variants +1.6 (all p<0.0001). Lower temp = higher specific productivity, longer duration, higher titer, slightly higher aFucosylation, slightly lower galactosylation.
pH -> aFuc -0.99, Galactosylation -2.43, Aggregates +0.4, Acidic Variants -2.1 (p<0.0001). Lower pH = higher specific productivity/duration/titer and slightly higher aFucosylation.
CO2 -> aFuc -0.53, Galactosylation -2.42, Acidic Variants -4.0 (p<0.0001).
Osmolality -> aFuc -0.75, Galactosylation -1.37, Acidic Variants -1.0 (p<0.0001).
Culture Duration -> aFuc -1.36, Galactosylation -3.76, HCP +2.0E5 ppm, DNA +4.7E2 ppm, Aggregates +0.3 (p<0.0001). Longer culture -> higher titer, lower aFuc, lower viability, higher HCP & DNA.

Significant two-way interactions: Temp*pH (aFuc -0.57, Galact +1.88, AV +1.1), Temp*Osmo (Galact +2.04), CO2*pH (aFuc -0.84, Galact +1.96, AV -0.4), CO2*Osmo (Galact +0.65), pH*Duration (aFuc +1.35, Galact +2.96, AV -0.3), Osmo*Duration (Galact +0.71), Temp*Duration (aFuc +0.32); quadratic pH*pH -1.09 on aFuc.

Design space is multivariate (non-linear, interacting): defined by four inequalities keeping aFucosylation 2-13%, Galactosylation 10-40%, plus Acidic Variants 20-40% and Soluble Aggregates 0-3% (Table 3.17). Defined via Predictive Bayesian Reliability approach; design space = region with >99% reliability all CQAs simultaneously in-spec (dark-red region Fig 3.6). Acidic variants and aggregate limits not exceeded within tested ranges.
N-1 seed DOE (Table 3.8): none of N-1 pH/DO/Temp affected production-bioreactor product quality; N-1 pH and temperature designated KPPs (impact peak VCC, viability, culture duration).

Worst-case linkage conditions for downstream clearance material (high DNA/HCP/aggregate): high pH, high Temp, high iVCC, late harvest -> rapid viability decline; highest HCP 1.3x10^6 ppm and aggregate 3.1% observed.

unit_operations.name: N-1 Seed Bioreactor (Step 2, last seed expansion) - context
unit_operations.purpose: Final seed expansion feeding the production bioreactor; characterized because prior mAb experience showed N-1 can potentially affect product quality. Seed steps otherwise excluded from design space.
cqas_impacted: none demonstrated (no impact on production-bioreactor product quality)

process_parameters.name: Temperature Set-Point

process_parameters.setpoint: 27 (Process 2; changed from 30 to account for liquid head); 30 (Process 1)
process_parameters.notes: No significant impact

process_parameters.name: Culture Duration
process_parameters.notes: Extended to allow increased seed density

param_cqa_relationships: Full-factorial DOE (2 L) on N-1 pH/DO/Temp: no impact on production-bioreactor product quality (aFuc, galactosylation, HCP, aggregate all p>0.2). pH and Temperature affect N-1/production process attributes (peak VCC, viability, culture duration) -> designated KPP.

unit_operations.name: Harvest / Clarification (Step 4)
unit_operations.purpose: Primary continuous disk-stack centrifugation to remove bulk cells/debris followed by secondary depth filtration; clarified bulk held under controlled conditions to a maximum hold time.
cqas_impacted: none (assumed no impact on product quality for the case study)

process_parameters.name: Centrifugation (disk-stack)
process_parameters.notes: Detailed risk analysis/optimization explicitly NOT included; assumed no product-quality impact. Impacts process performance (product yield/titer).

process_parameters.name: Depth Filtration
process_parameters.notes: Secondary clarification

process_parameters.nor: held to a maximum allowed time prior to further processing

process_parameters.name: Turbidity at Harvest
process_parameters.notes: Monitored, not a parameter

unit_operations.name: Protein A Affinity Chromatography (Step 5)
unit_operations.purpose: First chromatographic capture; immobilized Protein A resin binds mAb from clarified harvest; removes HCP/DNA/small molecules in flow-through/wash; low-pH elution sets up viral inactivation. No viral clearance claim.
unit_operations.scale: Bed height 10-30 cm; multi-cycle to process one harvest; qualified scale-down model (same bed height, linear velocity, load/wash/elution CV). Resin A (Vendor A) commercial; Resin B (Vendor B) qualified alternate.
cqas_impacted: (no significant effect on aggregate or acidic variants/deamidation)

process_parameters.name: Protein Load
process_parameters.notes: Significant impact on HCP; slightly higher pool impurities at high load

process_parameters.name: Elution Buffer pH
process_parameters.notes: Significant impact on HCP; increasing HCP at low pH; interacts with load and end-collection

process_parameters.name: Flow Rate (load)
process_parameters.notes: Significant impact on product yield (high flow x high load decreases yield)

process_parameters.name: End of Pool Collection
process_parameters.notes: Significant impact on product yield (with non-linear interaction)

process_parameters.name: Operating Temperature (entire step)
process_parameters.notes: Expected higher HCP and lower leached Protein A at low temperature; no significant effect confirmed

process_parameters.name: Cell culture (clarified harvest) viability
process_parameters.notes: Robust across wide feed inputs (HCP, DNA, titer, viability)

process_parameters.name: Load Concentration (titer)
process_parameters.notes: No impact/interaction; lower titer only displaces impurities -> lower pool impurities

process_parameters.name: Bed Height
process_parameters.notes: Low bed height + high load + high flow can decrease yield/increase impurities

process_parameters.name: Equilibration/Wash pH
process_parameters.notes: No significant effect (Tris/NaCl buffer)

process_parameters.name: Equilibration/Wash composition
process_parameters.notes: No significant effect

process_parameters.name: Resin lifetime (Resin A)
process_parameters.notes: Lifetime study to 250 cycles: yield 97%->90%, HCP stable ~6,500-9,500 ng/mg, aggregate ~2%, no change acidic variants

process_parameters.name: Resin lifetime (Resin B, alternate)
process_parameters.notes: Resin B ~2-fold higher leached Protein A but cleared downstream; slightly different design space

param_cqa_relationships: Multivariate DOE (19-run, 6-factor Res IV fractional factorial): Elution pH and Protein Load significantly impact HCP (Figure 4.2 response surface: HCP rises with higher protein load and lower elution pH; contour 2000->>10000 ppm). Both classified WC-CPP.
Protein load, flow rate, and end-collection (CV) significantly impact product yield (two main effects + non-linear interaction) -> flow rate and end-collection = KPP.
No significant effect of any parameter on aggregate or acidic variants -> other parameters = GPP. Pool concentration 2-20 g/L, below low-pH VI limit (35 g/L).
Step is robust to wide feedstock inputs; HCP output linked to downstream CEX/AEX capability (linkage model Section 4.7, Eq. 6).

unit_operations.name: Low-pH Viral Inactivation (Step 6)
unit_operations.purpose: Inactivate adventitious enveloped viruses in Protein A pool; pH adjusted to 3.5 with acetic acid, held at ambient 30-60 min, then adjusted to 5.0, filtered, held for CEX. Not a purification step; worst-case stability conditions studied.
unit_operations.scale: 30 mL lab model qualified across scales; Protein A pool <=20 g/L (design space max 35 g/L). Modular viral clearance from X/Y/Z-Mab.

process_parameters.name: pH
process_parameters.par: Acceptable range 3.2-4.0 (worst-case study low = 3.2; virus clearance 3.2-4.0). pH <3.1 causes antibody precipitation
process_parameters.notes: Narrow range; pH >4.0 not demonstrated to inactivate XMuLV within 60 min; pH <3.2 may aggregate. Lower pH enhances inactivation rate

process_parameters.name: Hold Time
process_parameters.par: Acceptable range 60-180 min (study 0-240; virus clearance 15-180). Max acceptable hold = 180 min
process_parameters.notes: Longer -> aggregation (2.5+/-0.2% at 180 min, 3-sigma 3.1%); shorter -> incomplete inactivation. CEX clears aggregate to ~1%

process_parameters.name: A-Mab (protein) Concentration
process_parameters.par: <= 35 g/L (worst case). Platform max seen 31 g/L
process_parameters.notes: Little/no effect on inactivation kinetics, aggregation or acidic variants

process_parameters.name: Temperature
process_parameters.notes: Lower temperature -> slightly lower inactivation rate at short time/higher pH

param_cqa_relationships: XMuLV inactivation kinetics (Figure 4.3, modular X/Y/Z-Mab): pH 3.2-4.0 for 60 min gives >6.6 LRF; slightly lower rate at lower temperature and higher pH; only minimally affected by protein concentration. Consistent >=6.5 LRF (values >6.5 are 'greater than', below LOD).

Worst-case product-quality study (Table 4.16): aggregate rises 1.8%->2.5% (0->180 min), 2.7% at 240 min; acidic species 10.7%->11.3% (180 min), 12.0% at 240 min. No significant quality impact up to 180 min -> no quality-linked parameters from stability standpoint.
In-process hold study: 35 g/L, 25 °C, 7 days -> no significant degradation (aggregate 1.8->2.1%).
Design space (Figure 4.4) = intersection of viral-clearance acceptable range and aggregation acceptable range on a pH vs time plot, constrained by temperature 15-25 °C.
pH classified CPP (narrow range, high consequence); time and temperature WC-CPP (readily controlled); protein concentration GPP.

unit_operations.name: Cation Exchange Chromatography (CEX, Step 7)
unit_operations.purpose: Strong CEX in bind-and-elute (step elution) to reduce aggregate to DS-acceptable levels and reduce HCP for AEX; also clears DNA and leached Protein A; charge/glycosylation variants unaffected. Some viral clearance but no claim.
unit_operations.scale: Bed height 20 +/- 3 cm; ambient temperature; load pH 5.0+/-0.2 acetate; multi-cycle allowed. Scale-down model qualified to 15,000 L (scale-up factor 33,000).
cqas_impacted: (acidic species slightly, not CQA; DNA & Protein A insensitive)

process_parameters.name: Protein Load
process_parameters.notes: Higher load decreases resolution, increases aggregate and HCP; interacts with wash conductivity (HCP) and elution pH (aggregate)

process_parameters.name: Load/Wash Conductivity
process_parameters.notes: Decrease in load/wash conductivity decreases HCP clearance; significant interaction with protein load on HCP

process_parameters.name: Elution Buffer pH
process_parameters.notes: Affects yield and impurity (aggregate) distribution; significant interaction with protein load and curvature with stop-collect on aggregate

process_parameters.name: Elution Stop Collect
process_parameters.notes: Extended stop-collect -> minor increase in pool aggregate; significant curvature

process_parameters.name: Elution Flow Rate
process_parameters.notes: High flow affects peak shape, minor aggregate impact; affects yield

process_parameters.name: Bed Height
process_parameters.par: low bed height studied univariate - no significant effect
process_parameters.notes: Minimal effect on residence time

process_parameters.name: Temperature
process_parameters.notes: No significant impact

process_parameters.name: Elution Start Collect
process_parameters.notes: Acidic variants elute at front; early start slightly increases this non-CQA

process_parameters.name: Load HCP (input)
process_parameters.notes: Higher input HCP raises output HCP

process_parameters.name: Resin Lifetime
process_parameters.par: 200 cycles (from prior mAbs; not run for A-Mab)
process_parameters.notes: No change in dynamic binding capacity to 200 cycles

param_cqa_relationships: Multivariate DOE (2^7-2 fractional factorial, 48 runs incl. quadratic runs; three feed lots low/mid/high HCP & aggregate): HCP impacted by protein load, wash conductivity, and input HCP, with significant protein-load x wash-conductivity interaction. Aggregate impacted by protein load, elution stop-collect, elution pH, and input aggregate, with significant load x elution-pH interaction and curvature (stop-collect, elution pH). Acidic species slightly by protein load (not modeled, non-CQA).
Yield modeled as function of protein load, stop-collect, load/wash conductivity, elution flow rate, elution pH; input HCP and aggregate had slight yield effect.
DNA and Protein A largely insensitive to CEX. Clearance factors (Table 4.20): aggregate 2-3x, HCP 50-100x.

Since no downstream aggregate-reduction step, worst-case load (linked to low-pH VI aggregate <=3.1%) confirmed CEX reduces aggregate to ~1% (below spec) across all conditions -> aggregate does not constrain CEX design space. HCP linked to Protein A/AEX via Section 4.7 model.

unit_operations.name: Anion Exchange Chromatography (AEX, Step 8)
unit_operations.purpose: Final purification, flow-through mode binding HCP/DNA/endotoxin while mAb passes through; removes HCP/DNA/Protein A/endotoxin to DS limits and provides a viral clearance claim (XMuLV, MVM). AEX membrane evaluated as alternate format.
unit_operations.scale: Bed height ~19-20 cm; linear flow 150-300 cm/hr (mfg 300); protein ~200 g/L resin; commercial bed volume 509 L (15,000 L; scale-up factor 34,140). Single cycle typical.

process_parameters.name: AEX Load pH
process_parameters.par: Quality design space 7.2-7.8 (DOE 7.2/7.5/7.8); viral clearance acceptable >= 7.0
process_parameters.notes: Impacts HCP removal and viral clearance; virus removal decreases as pH decreases

process_parameters.name: Equilibration/Wash 1 Buffer Conductivity
process_parameters.notes: Impacts HCP and aggregate; kept equal to load in VC studies

process_parameters.name: AEX Load Conductivity
process_parameters.notes: Virus removal decreases as conductivity increases; interacts with pH

process_parameters.name: Protein Load (AEX resin)
process_parameters.par: Quality design space 50-300 (DOE 46.3/164.4/293 mg/mL); viral clearance <= 300 mg/mL resin
process_parameters.notes: Viral clearance robust to load; VC studies used higher-than-process loads

process_parameters.name: Protein Load (AEX membrane, alternate)
process_parameters.notes: Virus removal equivalent to resin even at >10 g/mL

process_parameters.name: Operating Flow Rate
process_parameters.notes: VC studies at min bed height/residence time and >max flow (worst case)

process_parameters.name: Equilibration/Wash 1 Buffer pH
process_parameters.notes: Effect minor vs load pH

process_parameters.name: Peak Collection Start (A280)
process_parameters.notes: Worst-case (lowest UV) used in VC studies

process_parameters.name: Peak Collection End (A280)
process_parameters.notes: Slight impact on aggregate and yield

process_parameters.name: Protein Concentration in Load
process_parameters.notes: Little/no effect on virus removal (Figure 4.9, pH 7.0/15 mS/cm)

process_parameters.name: Load Buffering Salt System
process_parameters.notes: Little dependence of virus removal on salt system

process_parameters.name: Bed Height
process_parameters.par: set at minimum for VC worst case

process_parameters.name: Resin Lifetime
process_parameters.par: 150 cycles (from X/Y/Z-Mab; not run for A-Mab)
process_parameters.notes: No correlation of viral clearance with resin age up to 150 cycles

param_cqa_relationships: DOE-1 (fractional factorial, 19 runs, feed HCP 170 ng/mg worst case): HCP impacted by Equilibration/Wash 1 buffer conductivity and AEX load pH (Figure 4.6 - HCP rises at lower pH / higher conductivity). Aggregate slightly impacted by Equil/Wash 1 conductivity and peak-collection end. Acidic species slightly by load pH (non-CQA, not modeled). Yield modeled vs Equil/Wash 1 conductivity and peak-collection end.

Viral clearance (Figures 4.7-4.8, combined A/X/Y/Z-Mab): virus removal depends on load pH and conductivity with interaction - clearance decreases as pH decreases and conductivity increases; little dependence on buffering salt. In green zone LRF >= 5.5 (XMuLV) and >= 4.0 (MVM) consistently achieved; black zone (low pH/high conductivity) little removal.
Protein concentration in load has little/no effect on virus removal up to ~50 mg/mL (Figure 4.9); resin vs membrane equivalent.

Actual AEX quality design space (Table 4.31) is narrower than viral-clearance ranges; quality operation must run within narrower design space. Parameter classification set by final risk assessment (Cause & Effect matrix, scores >300 -> DOE-1).
Cannot determine full HCP design space in isolation - AEX linked with Protein A and CEX via algebraic HCP model (Section 4.7, Eq. 6).

unit_operations.name: Small Virus Retentive Filtration (Step 9)
unit_operations.purpose: Dedicated orthogonal virus removal by size exclusion/depth filtration ('Type-F' filter); removes small non-enveloped (MVM/PPV 18-24 nm) and larger enveloped (XMuLV 80-130 nm) viruses. Does not impact product quality other than virus load.
unit_operations.scale: Lab model scale-down factor 1,000-4,000; minimal flux decay to 124 L/m2; recovery >=98%. Modular claims from 4 mAbs incl. A-Mab.

process_parameters.name: Filtration Volume (Volumetric Load)
process_parameters.par: <= 105 L/m2 upper limit (incl. chase volume) for Type-F; breakthrough studied to 140 L/m2
process_parameters.notes: MVM LRF decreases with volume: fractions LRF >= 4.62 (0-105 L/m2) vs 3.91 (4th, 105-140 L/m2). No XMuLV breakthrough even above typical load. Chase ~1-3% of volume

process_parameters.name: Filtration Pressure
process_parameters.nor: manufacturer operating limits (studies at 13 psi constant pressure shown)
process_parameters.par: Filter Specific; VC studies run above operating limit but within manufacturer limit
process_parameters.notes: Pressure may matter for removal especially at high filtration volume; easy to control -> WC-CPP not CPP

process_parameters.name: Filter Integrity Test
process_parameters.notes: Critical procedural control per filter type

process_parameters.name: Chase Volume
process_parameters.notes: Identified with load and pressure as parameters potentially affecting removal

process_parameters.name: Buffer pH / Conductivity / Salt species
process_parameters.notes: Little/no dependence of virus removal on pH, conductivity, buffer salt

process_parameters.name: Protein Concentration
process_parameters.notes: Figure 4.14: no dependence of virus removal on protein concentration

param_cqa_relationships: Figures 4.13-4.14 (combined A/X/Y/Z-Mab): little/no dependence of XMuLV and MVM removal on protein concentration, buffer salt species, pH, or conductivity.

Figure 4.15: MVM LRF decreases as filtration volume increases; 4th fraction (105-140 L/m2) LRF 3.91 vs >=4.62 for first three fractions -> volumetric load <= 105 L/m2 selected as Type-F upper limit; classified WC-CPP.
XMuLV shows no breakthrough in any mAb process with this filter, even exceeding typical loads.

Design space (Table 4.34): Pressure and Filtration volume = WC-CPP (filter-specific, modular); integrity test = procedural control. Provides assurance of LRF >= 4.62 for both MVM and XMuLV regardless of buffer composition/pH/conductivity or protein up to 50 mg/mL.
No aggregation/fragmentation detected before/after filtration (Figure 4.12, ~98.5->98.6% by HPSEC); re-filtration acceptable after integrity failure.

unit_operations.name: Ultrafiltration / Diafiltration (UF/DF, Formulation Step)
unit_operations.purpose: Formulation and concentration of mAb to drug substance specification (e.g., 75 g A-Mab/L) via diafiltration and ultrafiltration.
unit_operations.scale: Input from SVRF 6-8 g/L -> DS ~75 g/L

process_parameters.name: UF/DF process parameters
process_parameters.notes: UF/DF process step explicitly NOT included in the case study downstream characterization; formulation studies are presented in the Drug Product (Chapter 5) section. Target DS concentration e.g. 75 g A-Mab/L. Transmembrane flux referenced only for the SVRF scale-down model, not UF/DF.

param_cqa_relationships: Not stated - step deliberately excluded from the drug-substance process characterization; no design space, DOE, or parameter classifications provided in Section 4.6.

notes: Source: refs/text/amab.txt (A-Mab Case Study, CMC Biotech Working Group). Upstream design space (Section 3.5) is built ONLY on the Production Bioreactor; seed steps 1-2 and Harvest are excluded (low quality risk). All Step-3 quality-linked parameters are WC-CPP (no CPPs upstream) because all are well controlled with reliable design space. Downstream: the ONLY CPP in the entire train is low-pH VI pH (narrow range). Everything else quality/virus-linked is WC-CPP; yield-only or robust parameters are KPP/GPP. Numeric design-space bounds for the bioreactor: pH 6.6-7.1, T 34-36 C, CO2 40-160 mmHg, Osmo 360-440 mOsm, culture duration 15-19 d (17 d optimal), with Bayesian >99% reliability. CQA limits (Table 3.17): aFuc 2-13%, Galactosylation 10-40%, Acidic Variants 20-40% (non-CQA, included for consistency), Soluble Aggregates 0-3%. Response-surface scaled estimates captured verbatim from Table 3.16 (per half-range). Two anticipated post-launch changes documented: alternate Protein A Resin B (Vendor B) and AEX resin->membrane. Downstream HCP handled via a linked multivariate model across Protein A/CEX/AEX (Section 4.7, Equation 6). Viral clearance claims: low-pH VI XMuLV >6.6 LRF; AEX XMuLV >=5.5 / MVM >=4.0 LRF; SVRF MVM & XMuLV >=4.62 LRF. Where the source states values only as 'not stated', 'Not Required', or 'data not shown', that is recorded rather than inferred. UF/DF and final filtration are explicitly out of scope of the DS characterization (Table 4.1). Note the source contains OCR/formatting artifacts in equation/figure blocks (pages 79-84, 90-92, 132, 138) - numeric axis fragments were interpreted against the accompanying table text where possible.
